learn.title: Who is the competent financial authority?
learn.summary: The person whose delegated powers cover the full value of the case.
learn.text: The competent financial authority (CFA) is the authority whose delegated ceiling for that schedule item covers the full value of the case. If the value is above the CO's ceiling, the case goes up, complete, to the next level. Sanctioning beyond your powers is one of the most common audit findings.

learn.title: What does IFA concurrence mean?
learn.summary: Some powers can only be used after the finance adviser agrees.
learn.text: For some schedule items and values, the CFA can only sanction after the Integrated Financial Adviser concurs. The schedule says which. Plan for it: the IFA will ask about necessity, the budget head, availability of funds, the procurement route and the basis of the price.

learn.title: Allotment, commitment, expenditure
learn.summary: Why the balance in your register is usually wrong.
learn.text: Allotment is what you were given. Commitment is what you have promised through orders not yet paid. Expenditure is what accounts have booked. Units that track only payments think they have more money than they do until February.

learn.title: What counts as splitting a demand?
learn.summary: Breaking one need into small buys to stay under a ceiling.
learn.text: If several purchases are really one requirement, such as the same item for different sub-units in the same month, they are judged at their combined value. Buying them separately to stay within a lower authority's powers is splitting, and it is not permitted.

learn.title: When must I use GeM?
learn.summary: If the item is on GeM, start there.
learn.text: If the goods or services are available on the Government e-Marketplace, buy through GeM. The buying mode on GeM depends on the value. Record a reason if you buy outside GeM.

learn.title: Which purchase mode fits my value?
learn.summary: No quotation, committee, limited tender, open tender.
learn.text: Under the revised GFR bands reported in 2025: up to ₹2 lakh without quotation; above ₹2 lakh to ₹25 lakh through a three-member purchase committee; up to ₹1 crore through limited tender; above ₹1 crore through an advertised tender. DPM 2025 may set defence-specific procedure on top of this.

learn.title: Lapse and surrender
learn.text: Funds not spent by 31 March lapse. If you know you will not use money, surrender it early so someone else can. Large lapses are often read as 'the unit did not need it', and next year's allotment can shrink.

learn.title: Proprietary items and single tender
learn.text: If only one firm makes what you need, you can use a single tender with a proprietary article certificate and a recorded reason. The price is then negotiated by a contract negotiation committee.
